principles.name: laziness-protocol
principles.title: Laziness Protocol
principles.applies_when: Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add a layer. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves it.

principles.name: foundational-thinking
principles.title: Foundational Thinking
principles.applies_when: Before writing logic. Settle core types, data structures, and what concurrent actors share first.

principles.name: redesign-from-first-principles
principles.title: Redesign from First Principles
principles.applies_when: A new requirement lands in an existing design. Redesign as if it had been there from day one.

principles.name: attack-the-premise
principles.title: Attack the Premise
principles.applies_when: Two fixes sharing one premise failed. Write the premise down and test it before a third fix.

principles.name: subtract-before-you-add
principles.title: Subtract Before You Add
principles.applies_when: Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.

principles.name: minimize-reader-load
principles.title: Minimize Reader Load
principles.applies_when: Code is hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.

principles.name: outcome-oriented-execution
principles.title: Outcome-Oriented Execution
principles.applies_when: Planned rewrites and migrations. Converge on the target design; skip throwaway compatibility states.

principles.name: experience-first
principles.title: Experience First
principles.applies_when: Product, UX, or scope tradeoffs. Choose what the user feels over implementation convenience.

principles.name: exhaust-the-design-space
principles.title: Exhaust the Design Space
principles.applies_when: A novel interaction or architecture with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes, then compare.

principles.name: build-the-lever
principles.title: Build the Lever
principles.applies_when: Any non-trivial work. Build the script, codemod, or check that does or proves it, so a reviewer can rerun it.

principles.name: model-the-domain
principles.title: Model the Domain
principles.applies_when: Stateful or branch-heavy logic. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, table, typed model).

principles.name: boundary-discipline
principles.title: Boundary Discipline
principles.applies_when: Wiring validation, errors, or adapters. Guard at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep logic pure.

principles.name: type-system-discipline
principles.title: Type System Discipline
principles.applies_when: Designing types or signatures. Make illegal states unrepresentable and parse external data at boundaries.

principles.name: make-operations-idempotent
principles.title: Make Operations Idempotent
principles.applies_when: Commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that face crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.

principles.name: migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
principles.title: Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs
principles.applies_when: A new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate every caller and delete the old API in one wave.

principles.name: separate-before-serializing-shared-state
principles.title: Separate Before Serializing Shared State
principles.applies_when: Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, or key. Remove the sharing before adding locks.

principles.name: prove-it-works
principles.title: Prove It Works
principles.applies_when: Before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact on the real surface, not a proxy.

principles.name: fix-root-causes
principles.title: Fix Root Causes
principles.applies_when: Debugging. Trace each symptom to the first wrong state and fix it there; a guard is not a fix.

principles.name: sequence-verifiable-units
principles.title: Sequence Work into Verifiable Units
principles.applies_when: Multi-step work and commit stacks. Small units that each end in a check, verified before the next.

principles.name: test-behavior-not-implementation
principles.title: Test Behavior, Not Implementation
principles.applies_when: Writing or keeping a test. Assert what users observe, so it fails only when behavior breaks.

principles.name: explain-the-number
principles.title: Explain the Number
principles.applies_when: Before trusting or reporting a measurement. Find what limits it and rule out measuring the wrong thing.

principles.name: guard-the-context-window
principles.title: Guard the Context Window
principles.applies_when: Large outputs, long files, fan-out. Route bulk to subagents or files; keep summaries in the main thread.

principles.name: never-block-on-the-human
principles.title: Never Block on the Human
principles.applies_when: Tempted to ask about reversible work. Proceed, show the result, let the human course-correct.

principles.name: encode-lessons-in-structure
principles.title: Encode Lessons in Structure
principles.applies_when: Writing the same instruction twice. Encode it as a lint, test, type, or script instead of more text.
